hints: Focus on the alcohol type, since only one class of alcohol can be oxidised to a ketone.
Look at the carbon carrying the -OH group in each name, a 1-ol is usually primary but a 2-ol can be secondary or tertiary depending on branching.
Pick out the secondary alcohol where the -OH carbon still has one hydrogen to lose, then it will form a C=O in the middle of the chain under reflux.
walkthrough:
**Recall the oxidation rules for alcohols**

Remember, acidified dichromate(VI) is a strong oxidising agent, supplied as [O]. The outcome depends on the alcohol class.

$$\text{primary alcohol} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{aldehyde} \xrightarrow{[O], reflux} \text{carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{secondary alcohol} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{ketone}$$
$$\text{tertiary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$

**Classify each alcohol by the -OH carbon**

Count how many other carbons are joined to the C-OH carbon. One means primary, two means secondary, three means tertiary.

$\text{pentan-1-ol: CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is primary.

$\text{2-methylbutan-1-ol: CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{OH}$ is primary, the -OH is on $\text{C1}$.

$\text{2-methylbutan-2-ol: CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$ is tertiary, the -OH carbon joins three other carbons.

**Spot the secondary alcohol that gives a ketone**

$\text{3-methylbutan-2-ol}$ is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$. The $\text{C2}$ with -OH joins two other carbons, so it is secondary.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3 + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
That product, 3-methylbutan-2-one, is a ketone, and it resists further oxidation.

options.A: Pentan-1-ol is a primary alcohol. With acidified dichromate under reflux it first forms pentanal and then is further oxidised to pentanoic acid, not a ketone.
options.B: 2-methylbutan-1-ol has the -OH on C1, so it is still a primary alcohol despite the branching. It oxidises to an aldehyde then a carboxylic acid under reflux, not a ketone.
options.C: 2-methylbutan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol. The C-OH carbon has no hydrogen to lose and is joined to three alkyl groups, so it is resistant to oxidation and gives no reaction.
options.D: 3-methylbutan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol because the C2 bearing -OH is joined to two other carbons. Oxidation removes the one H from that carbon to give the ketone 3-methylbutan-2-one, which cannot be oxidised further.
